query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing traditional static EAM references with an actively learned machine‐learning interatomic potential (ML‐IAP) that is iteratively trained on ab initio configurations spanning both solid and liquid states at high melting temperatures will better represent the diverse atomic configurations of the liquid. This substitution should improve the reference–target phase‐space overlap and reduce the thermodynamic‐integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (HEAs) in both their solid and liquid phases at and near their high melting temperatures (e.g., refractory HEAs such as HfNbTaTiZr or similar systems with >4 principal elements)
generation.intervention: Replace the conventional static EAM potentials with a machine-learning potential (e.g., a neural network or Gaussian approximation potential) that is actively and iteratively trained using ab initio molecular dynamics snapshots collected from high-temperature simulations including both solid and liquid states
generation.conditions: Applicable for HEAs with significant configurational complexity and high melting points (temperatures from approximately 0.9T_m up to T_m, where T_m > 1500 °C) in both the solid and liquid phase; simulations should span a range of configurations representative of high-temperature disorder
generation.structural_mediator: The ML potential embeds representations of local atomic environments across a wide distribution of coordination numbers and bonding arrangements, effectively capturing many-body interactions characteristic of high-temperature disorder
generation.mechanism: By dynamically learning from an extensive set of ab initio configurations, the ML potential captures the full breadth of atomic configurations—especially those in the disordered liquid state—that static EAM potentials miss. This enhanced representation increases phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems, thereby reducing the mismatch during thermodynamic integration
generation.predicted_outcome: The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is predicted to decrease by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references. This reduction will be observable as a smoother integration pathway with fewer sampling points needed and improved free-energy agreement with ab initio benchmarks
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD’s EAM reference approach, which is known to inadequately capture the wide array of atomic configurations in the high-temperature liquid state and thus result in larger integration path mismatches
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective only for complex HEAs exhibiting high configurational entropy and in the temperature regime where liquid disorder dominates (near melting). Its advantages may be less pronounced in simpler alloys or at lower temperatures where atomic configurations are less diverse
generation.uncertainty: The estimated 20–30% reduction in mismatch is approximate since direct benchmarks for ML potentials in complex HEA liquid states are limited; further validations across different compositions and temperature regimes are needed

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct parallel thermodynamic integration simulations on a representative HEA (e.g., HfNbTaTiZr) at temperatures near melting using both (a) the standard TOR-TILD EAM reference method and (b) the newly developed ML potential. Evaluate the smoothness of the integration curve, the number of integration points required, and the free energy computed along the pathway against direct ab initio free-energy benchmarks.
measurements: Variance and convergence behavior of free-energy estimates
Phase-space overlap metrics (e.g., distribution of local atomic environments)
Direct comparison of computed free energies with ab initio benchmarks
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML potential fails to decrease the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least approximately 20–30% relative to the EAM-based TOR-TILD method, or if free-energy estimates are not in significantly better agreement with ab initio benchmarks, then the hypothesis will be rejected
